pr_title: DOC: Docstring script to not require ending period for bullet points
pr_body:
- [X] closes #25461
- [X] passes `git diff upstream/master -u -- "*.py" | flake8 --diff`

This PR tries to solve the issue #25461 .

I thought that the validator should check that the last line of the parameter description is a part of a bullet point before raising the error PR09.

In order to do that, I had to add an extra method in the Docstring class that return a parameter description line by line (in a list). This is because Docstring.parameter_desc() returns the description as 1 string.

Please let me know how I can improve this or if I did not consider something.

issue_context.title: Fix Validation Script to Not Error Out if Bullet Points Don't End with Period
issue_context.body:
Quite a few PRs lately have worked around the validation script error of descriptions not ending with a period when there are bullet points by adding periods to the end of each bullet point. This looks tacky and is really just a hack to get around the validator failing.

Would rather update the validator to maybe ignore bullet points as part of the description, though @datapythonista may have other thoughts.

xref #20298
comments:
This could be as simple as removing two lines from the validator:
```
if doc.parameter_desc(param)[-1] != '.':
  errs.append(error('PR09', param_name=param))
```

This solution is effectively the same as removing error code PR09.

Is this the outcome you're looking for? Or are there cases in which you want the validator to complain about bullets not ending in periods?

review_comments: I think this first paragraph is unnecessary. Also, we start docstrings in the next line after the quotes.

```suggestion
BULLET_LIST_PATTERN = re.compile(r"(\*|-|\+|•|‣|⁃)\s+.*")
```

I think should add `+` for the whitespace. Is there a reason for the positive lookbehind?

I'd prefer to call this `param_desc_ends_with_period`.

Also, I'd pass `param_name` and `param_desc` and avoid calling `self.parameter_desc` from this function.

I don't think we ever use anything but `-` and `*` for bullet points. Is this expression working?

I feel like it'd be simpler to simply check if the last line starts by `..`, `*`, `-` or is more indented than the rest of the docstring. If it does skip the check for ending with a period. I think this should capture most of the cases, if not all.

Hi @datapythonista, thank your for all the suggestions.

I have included all those bullets points because it was suggested in a comment above.

Also I think I have implemented something similar to your suggestion in few commits before (everything before and including this commit https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/25786/commits/331e518387c161e73889164a70e348130fb4cfe1 )
Should I revert to this implementation?

@WillAyd I guess you suggested the regex approach. Not sure if I'm missing something, but I feel it's not feasible to capture whether the end of the parameter description is a list or a directive, in a simple way. Is it numpydoc preprocessing the value and making it easy, or do you think we can detect line breaks since the bullet point...?
I'm not tied to it if there's a better way. I just think the original incarnation here had too many loops, so fine with whatever strikes a readable balance you may know of

Thanks @WillAyd, I agree that this shouldn't need a complex implementation with loops.

@EdAbati do you mind pasting here what is the value we get for the parameter description of the docstring in the `parameters_with_bullet_points1` test?

My guess is that we can just validate that the last line doesn't start with:
- `*` or `-`
- `..`
- 4 spaces

If it doesn't, we require the final period, if it does, we don't require it.

Does it make sense?

Hi both,

@datapythonista the `parameter_desc` method applied to `parameters_with_bullet_points1` returns:
```
OrderedDict([('method',
              ("{'min', 'max'}, default 'min'",
               "Parameter introduction:* 'min': the description for min* 'max': the description for max that can also be very long and  requires an extra row"))])
```
I thought to use the `.doc["Parameters"] ` method of the `NumpyDocString` class just so we could access the parameter description line by line (as a list) and assess the last line. Is there another way to do this?

I guess we join all the lines ourselves, I guess we can return the list, or however numpydoc returns this, and just join where we need it (I guess we don't use this description in many places).

Btw, we're moving this script to numpydoc, we'll have to make this changes there, once https://github.com/numpy/numpydoc/pull/238 is merged (quite soon).
Ok, no problem I will close this for now. Thank you for the useful feedback

Are directives included in `self.parameter_desc`? The way this is written it really just checks if there is a bullet point somewhere in the description, but without regarding the position. I thought something with `re.findall` would be more appropriate just not sure how complicated that gets with directives

Hi @WillAyd , thank you for this and apologies again for the late reply.
`self.parameter_desc` returns the parameter docstring as 1 string removing everything after a directive.

For example, this method:
```
method : {'min', 'max'}, default 'min'
   Parameter introduction:

   * 'min': the description for min
   * 'max': the description for max

   .. versionadded:: 0.1.2
   .. deprecated:: 0.00.0
        A description
```
will be simply returned as 
`"Parameter introduction:* 'min': the description for min* 'max': the description for max"`

Since the newline characters (and blank lines) are also lost using `self.parameter_desc`, I am finding tricky to come up with a regex that perfectly matches a bullet list. Do you have anything in mind?
